name: CatchUp Showdown
desc: Multiplayer 3D Co-op friendslop rage game. Play catch to climb a tower, lose the ball and start again, while wacky environment mechanics make things interesting. Pitched, built and shipped in 2 months. Lead designer, systems and gameplay programmer on a four person core team; Releasing at Steam Next Fest: October 2026. Demo currently live
bullets: Deterministic level system where the entire tower is a pure function of two networked values so late joiners rebuild a bit-identical world with minimal network load
Host-authoritative scoring pipeline: quality weights, a convex reward curve, and a catalog of 25+ detectable tricks broadcast to a networked score banner
Crowd trick-request mechanic where the crowd demands a specific trick, and success or failure feeds back into the level by increasing/decreasing difficulty
Hazard roster: 10 unique environment mechanics, ballistic bomb turrets, matched slippery/sticky slime pipes that coat both players and the ball, and a spotlight musical-chairs target
Networked announcer-bot NPC driven by a PD spring with a three-layer mover/brain/mood state machine, reacting live to catches, misses, and climb height
Custom URP shaders and render features: screen-space level-transition wipes, silhouette shadow projection, tile glow, tinted decals, and a Shader Graph combo-fire HUD effect
Editor tooling: a Tower Balance window for stage authoring and churn curves, plus an edit-mode scroll preview that drives the real level pipeline
Player progression and meta: local coin economy, gacha cosmetic unlocks, and AES/HMAC-signed save data synced through Steam Cloud
Fully hand-authored uGUI main menu, pause menu, HUD and in-game shop with full controller navigation, leaderboards, and an event-driven friends list wired to Steam lobby visibility
Photon Fusion client-side for prediction, interpolation, and aim raycasting against rendered versus simulated physics poses

name: Swipers
desc: Asymmetric co-op multiplayer heist game. One player claims the Operator role and works a multi-screen station — live map, camera feeds, and the only copies of the per-run security manuals — while the rest of the crew robs procedurally generated facilities under deliberately clumsy physics. Systems and gameplay programmer on a two-developer team; paused when the team pivoted to a new project.
bullets: Designed and built the full guard AI stack: component-based state machine, dual-zone vision sensors, and data-driven guard archetypes authored as ScriptableObjects
Audio-driven stealth perception: piped live FMOD events and Photon Voice mic amplitude into guard hearing
Line-of-sight-aware pursuit with heading projection, movement-based detection rates, and a habituation system that turns repeated noise into masked dead zones
Data-driven guard spawning and routing: role ScriptableObjects, NavMesh waypoint generation, and context-sensitive route queries with SceneView preview tooling
Multi-component physics vacuum: Grabbable, draggable, pushable machine with separate PD-spring nozzle, Verlet-rope hose with procedural mesh generation, and a networked capacity-limited loot bag

Gadget framework with a six-slot input override system, plus over 12 gadgets built on it including a throwable teleporter portal, slow-motion beam gun, AI decoy, guard-stunning magazine, repair spray, 'wet floor sign' guard obstruction, and more

Operator "Man in the Chair" station: multi-screen workstation, live map markers and interactive map features, networked guard-identification puzzles, a custom URP render feature for the arcade X-ray tool, remote camera operation, remote player camera viewport, and more
FMOD integrated voice comms separating communication with the Operator into it's own 2D channel, while other players stay 3D with eachother
Diegetic 3D UI: a holographic mission-select table and a five-screen main menu workstation with render-texture input routing for UI Toolkit
Photon Fusion netcode: debugging and tuning client prediction and rollback desyncs across movement, physics, and animation, plus three-layer disconnect protection with deadlock recovery

name: Card Clash Auto Battler
desc: A Super Auto Pets–inspired auto battler card game. Draft a lineup, equip boosters, and battle head-to-head in local 2-player PvP or against AI bots. 100+ cards with unique abilities, synergies, and set-collection bonuses. Built solo as a browser game.
bullets: 112-card roster spanning characters, ships, trails, emotes, and landmarks, each with unique stats and abilities
Set-collection bonuses that buff themed groups when fielded together
Local 2-player PvP plus AI bot opponents across a 5-round match
Custom deck builder with localStorage-saved lineups

name: Scraptics
desc: A tactical turn-based roguelike on a hex grid with a unique inventory puzzle mechanic. Pitched in an internal game jam, greenlit for full production, and led as programmer, designer, and team lead for 3 years at Halfbrick Studios. Shipped to closed beta on iOS and Android.
bullets: Architected the full systems stack: turn management, hex-grid logic, roguelike progression, and inventory puzzle systems
Wrote complex recursive algorithms powering the core puzzle mechanic
Designed and programmed modular enemy AI behavior systems
Developed custom editor tools to support content creation and team workflows
Built full UI/UX across all game screens and menus
Cross-platform iOS & Android builds with profiling and performance optimization
Leaderboard networking and metadata architecture using Unity Cloud Services
Cross-platform save systems
Led a team of 4 developers across the full production lifecycle

name: Sumo Fight
desc: Multiplayer beat-em-up party game built in one week. Lead programmer on a team of 5.
bullets: Photon networking for player customization sync and core gameplay

name: Survivors Aren't Dead
desc: Survivor-like action game built in one week. Pitched the concept, led the project, and served as lead programmer on a team of 4.
bullets: Created the pitch and core design document
Lead programmer, enemy behavior programmer, and sound designer

name: Unannounced Mobile Project
desc: A 2D side-scrolling endless runner with a novel physics-driven swinging mechanic. Created the prototype that was greenlit, then led the project until it was paused due to shifting company priorities.
bullets: Created the original prototype establishing the core loop and swinging mechanic
Led physics prototyping and mechanical iteration
Project lead and lead programmer for a team of 4

name: Rucksack Dungeon
desc: The prototype that became Scraptics. Built in one week at an internal Halfbrick game jam, greenlit for full production, and reworked into the full game over the following 3 years. Team lead and AI behavior programmer.
bullets: Designed and implemented AI enemy behaviour systems
Team lead across the full jam week
Prototype was selected and greenlit — became the foundation for Scraptics

name: To The Moon!
desc: Competitive 3D space dogfighter. Capstone project at Full Sail University. Project lead on a team of 6.
bullets: AI fighter ships using steering behaviors and compute shaders for improved framerate at scale
Full Photon networking stack: GameManager, MatchManager, weapons, projectiles, loading transitions, procedural map generation
All multiplayer UI: ready-up system, name changing, lobby/player listing, scoreboard, score tracking, and hit registration
Player controller with single/multiplayer versions via polymorphism and inheritance

name: Memoria Damnum
desc: 2D platformer built in 48 hours for Global Game Jam 2020. Programming lead on a team of 9.
bullets: Object pooling system for collectibles with persistent collection state
Contributed to level design, audio systems, GameManager architecture, and VFX

name: Retrospectre
desc: Retrowave-inspired 2.5D metroidvania platformer. Project lead on a team of 4.
bullets: AI systems for 8+ distinct enemy types with varied behaviors and attack patterns
Player controller, weapon systems, and projectile mechanics
Level design and all interactable systems: destructible areas, climbable walls, moving platforms, environmental puzzles
